clean_story:
"Text on paper. Word puts it on screen.

The name 'Word' fits its purpose: it turns typed letters into digital text, just like a pen turns thoughts into ink.

Most see Word as a blank page waiting for words. Few notice how it silently shapes those words—auto-correcting typos like a vigilant editor, aligning margins like an invisible ruler, or embedding fonts so a document looks the same on any computer. It’s not just typing; it’s precision engineering for language. A writer drafting a novel might never think about the .docx file quietly tracking every revision, or the 'Styles' tool that lets them reformat 200 pages with one click. Even a simple letter benefits from Word’s ability to count words, check grammar, or turn bullet points into a table with two keystrokes. No other tool makes text this adaptable, portable, and professional without requiring design skills.

Three related subjects are digital typography, document collaboration, and text encoding."
